behavior: The exact authenticated sampler plan and sealed registered-array program form one immutable aggregate proof; checked demand is H+N+safety with no caller-provided byte-proof constructor.
Both live source owners are validated under the same usage lock before one existing-ledger destination commit. Rejection precedes history allocation and native work.
The aggregate initializes one fresh destination identity, two distinct scopes, and matching H holds in the ledger and closed host custody. Native adoption cannot spend retained history funding.
Frozen host payload and native work have independent retirement. Closing arrays first keeps the host source valid; dropping host first cannot certify native work or clear quarantine.
The existing admitted native worker consumes the aggregate scope without a second reservation, retains partial results through recovery, and publishes only completed destination storage.
Saved numerical duplication authenticates its own host account/native roots after the original run advances or retires; it neither requires nor replays the old live receipt/frontier.

TextSnapshotBackend now separates saved sampler/input data from live sampling state. Full snapshot capture uses one aggregate hook; restore/fork stage one independent runnable pair before installation.

MLX bounded Standard/Mirostat component copies preserve history capacity, adaptive controls, stochastic key and scalar values. Escaped immutable owners and native aliases retain appropriate independent charges.
Funded saved state cannot be converted into runnable sampling or stripped into unquoted copies. The production trait rejects those operations before mutation/copying and preserves source accounting.
Existing unquoted shared snapshot, controller, Unicode, restore/fork, admission and recovery behavior remains covered.
limits: The aggregate covers canonical sampler payload plus native key/scalar copy workspace. Full native state/layout/cache identity, controller, decoder, capture and delivery payloads still need their complete source-bound plans.

Bounded prefill-input copying and funded runnable restore/fork remain implementation work. The latter requires fresh resumed-run admission, initial-decode permission and installed-state revision binding; saved data grants none.
Whole finite snapshots retain early host-exclusion rejection until their remaining payloads can join the aggregate before allocation.
Host/native component diagnostics overlap within one account and must not be summed as separate charges. Runtime/allocator bookkeeping and process/system memory are not included.
Three external checkpoint fixtures remain ignored. No new released-checkpoint, distributed numerical, multi-host or process/allocator-peak measurement was performed.
Full family/path bounded inference goal remains incomplete.
